$$\text{RHS}=\dfrac{\operatorname{cosec}A}{\operatorname{cosec}A-\sin A}=\operatorname{cosec}A\div\left(\operatorname{cosec}A-\sin A\right)=\dfrac{1}{\sin A}\div\left(\dfrac{1}{\sin A}-\sin A\right)$$

$$=\dfrac{1}{\sin A}\div\dfrac{1-\sin^2A}{\sin A}$$

but $\cos^2A+\sin^2A=1$, so $\cos^2A=1-\sin^2A$

$$=\dfrac{1}{\sin A}\times\dfrac{\sin A}{\cos^2A}=\dfrac{1}{\cos^2A}=\sec^2A$$

$\text{RHS}=\text{LHS}$

Or:

$$\text{LHS}=\sec^2A=1+\tan^2A=1+\dfrac{\sin^2A}{\cos^2A}=1+\dfrac{\sin^2A}{1-\sin^2A}=\dfrac{1-\sin^2A+\sin^2A}{1-\sin^2A}$$

$$=\dfrac{1}{1-\sin^2A}=\dfrac{\frac{1}{\sin A}}{\frac{1}{\sin A}-\frac{\sin^2A}{\sin A}}=\dfrac{\operatorname{cosec}A}{\operatorname{cosec}A-\sin A}=\text{RHS}$$

$$A_{\text{photo}}=(x-4)(y-2)=20\implies y-2=\dfrac{20}{x-4}$$

$$y=\dfrac{20}{x-4}+2=\dfrac{20+2(x-4)}{x-4}=\dfrac{20+2x-8}{x-4}=\dfrac{12+2x}{x-4}$$

$$A=x\times y=x\times\dfrac{12+2x}{x-4}=\dfrac{12x+2x^2}{x-4}=\dfrac{2x^2+12x}{x-4}$$

OR let the width of the photo be $y$: $A_{\text{photo}}=(x-4)\times y=20$, so $y=\dfrac{20}{x-4}$.

$$A=x(y+2)=x\left(\dfrac{20}{x-4}+2\right)=x\times\dfrac{20+2(x-4)}{x-4}=x\times\dfrac{20+2x-8}{x-4}=\dfrac{x(12+2x)}{x-4}=\dfrac{12x+2x^2}{x-4}=\dfrac{2x^2+12x}{x-4}$$

For $\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}(3\sin 2x-3\sin 2a)\,dx=0$ it is required that

$$\int_0^a(3\sin 2a-3\sin 2x)\,dx=\int_a^{\frac{\pi}{4}}(3\sin 2x-3\sin 2a)\,dx$$

$$\left[3x\sin 2a-\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\cos 2x\right)\right]_0^a=\left[-\dfrac{3}{2}\cos 2x-3x\sin 2a\right]_a^{\frac{\pi}{4}}$$

$$3a\sin 2a+\dfrac{3}{2}\cos 2a-\left(0+\dfrac{3}{2}\cos 0\right)=-\dfrac{3}{2}\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\sin 2a-\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\cos 2a-3a\sin 2a\right)$$

$$3a\sin 2a+\dfrac{3}{2}\cos 2a-\dfrac{3}{2}=-\dfrac{3}{2}\times 0-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\sin 2a+\dfrac{3}{2}\cos 2a+3a\sin 2a$$

$$-\dfrac{3}{2}=-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\sin 2a$$

$$y=\dfrac{x^3}{6}+\dfrac{x^2}{4}-3x+1$$

$$y'=\dfrac{3x^2}{6}+\dfrac{2x}{4}-3$$

Stationary points occur when $y'=0$:

$$0=\dfrac{x^2}{2}+\dfrac{x}{2}-3=\dfrac{1}{2}(x^2+x-6)=\dfrac{1}{2}(x+3)(x-2)$$

$x=-3$: $y=\dfrac{-27}{6}+\dfrac{9}{4}+9+1=\dfrac{31}{4}=7\dfrac{3}{4}$

$x=2$: $y=\dfrac{8}{6}+\dfrac{4}{4}-6+1=-\dfrac{8}{3}=-2\dfrac{2}{3}$

$$y''=x+\dfrac{1}{2}$$

When $x=-3$, $y''=-3+\dfrac{1}{2}=-2\dfrac{1}{2}<0$: maximum turning point at $\left(-3,\,7\dfrac{3}{4}\right)$

When $x=2$, $y''=2+\dfrac{1}{2}=2\dfrac{1}{2}>0$: minimum turning point at $\left(2,\,-2\dfrac{2}{3}\right)$

Possible points of inflexion when $y''=0$: $x+\dfrac{1}{2}=0$, $x=-\dfrac{1}{2}$,

$$y=\dfrac{-1}{8\times 6}+\dfrac{1}{4\times 4}-3\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)+1=-\dfrac{1}{48}+\dfrac{1}{16}+\dfrac{3}{2}+1=\dfrac{61}{24}=2\dfrac{13}{24}\approx 2.5416$$

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} x & -1 & -\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ \hline y'' & -\frac{1}{2} & 0 & \frac{1}{2} \end{array}$$

There is a change in concavity, $\therefore$ there is a point of inflexion at $\left(-\dfrac{1}{2},\,2\dfrac{13}{24}\right)$.
